BiblicalUsage: Namer is a leopard, spotted and swift, and it is used for the speed of an army and the watchfulness of a judge. In Habakkuk 1:8 the horses of the Chaldeans are swifter than the leopards and more fierce than the evening wolves, and in Hosea 13:7 the Lord says He will be to Israel as a leopard by the way, watching them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the leopard is feared for the same reason in both verses: it is fast, it is spotted, and it is already watching; an enemy you cannot outrun and a God you cannot hide from wear the same picture.
